script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this is form-only. KC has been the functional offense (Walker 47 carries for 290, Kelce 16 targets for 172) and Mahomes' EPA/dropback vs blitz is 0.36 (n=24) into MIA's 41% blitz, so the base case is KC moving the ball, Walker handling early carries, and Kelce working the middle where MIA allows 11.27 YPA. KC has allowed only 2 passes of 20+ on 63 attempts and MIA's QB is -0.50 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=18) against a 32% KC blitz, so Miami is more likely to trail and fail on explosives than to dictate pace.
script.flip1: Shootout or Miami hangs around: KC carry share dips, Walker rush yards stall, and the passing game (Kelce, Rice 8/102, Thornton 5/86 on 121 air yards; Miami Washington 13/96 on 162 air yards and Douglas 10/113) becomes the path. Walker rush+rec can still live off his 16 targets if the 41% blitz keeps producing checkdowns.
script.flip2: KC gets up big and clocks it with Walker, so his rush line lives while Kelce and Thornton yards stall, and Miami abandons the run so Achane (31 carries, 110 yards, 3.55 YPC) and Willis (8 carries, 45 yards) rush unders become the Miami side of that script.

market_rung_price: Main lines only; no alt rungs in the pack, and short-priced alts are not used. Travis Kelce recyds over 52.5 -113.5 (efficiency/matchup edge into the middle, not a receptions market). Kenneth Walker rushrecyds over 109.5 -113.5 rather than rushyds over 85.5, because MIA's 3.95 YPC allowed is not a weak run defense and the 41% blitz is a receiving-volume path the combined market captures. Achane rushrecyds 93 is listed at +nan and is not priced, so it is not a leg.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost because the two-game samples were noise: Miami's middle 11.27 YPA came on only 15 attempts and they took Kelce away, holding him under 5 targets while Worthy (13 targets, 82 air yards) and Thornton (121 air yards) took the explosives Miami has allowed (6 of 52), and a clock-killing KC lead never let Kelce reach 52.5. Walker ran into a real 3.95 YPC defense, the unsaved spread meant KC was never confirmed as the leading side, his carries were cut, and 11 air yards of checkdown receiving did not replace the lost rush yards, so 109.5 rush+rec missed. That counter is small-sample regression plus an unknown spread; it is not stronger than the logged target share, carry share, and blitz EPA split, so neither leg is dropped.
slip_story: One story only: KC's offense functions against a 41% blitz and attacks Miami's middle while Walker keeps the touches. Kelce recyds over and Walker rushrecyds over win together in that script and in a pass-heavier flip; Kelce is the leg that dies if KC purely clocks it with Walker. Do not mix in a game under, Miami explosive overs, or TDs/receptions. Read is pre-kickoff only and is not locked, hashed, or graded (step 12 not runnable from this pack).
